result:
The bracket is modelled and all four files exported without errors.

The model is in a FreeCAD document called `Bracket`. The width is the `Width` cell in a spreadsheet called `Params`. The plate lengths and both hole positions are driven from that cell. The holes sit at X = Width/2 ± 20 and Z = 35.

| Export | Files | Bounding box (X × Y × Z) | Hole centres (X) | Volume |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Width 80 | `/lab/out/bracket-80.step`, `/lab/out/bracket-80.stl` | 0–80 × 0–60 × 0–50 | 20 and 60 | 33 762.9 mm³ |
| Width 100 | `/lab/out/bracket-100.step`, `/lab/out/bracket-100.stl` | 0–100 × 0–60 × 0–50 | 30 and 70 | 42 242.9 mm³ |

I changed `Width` from 80 to 100 and recomputed. The holes stayed centred. The volume at width 80 matches a hand calculation, and the shape checked valid at both widths.

**One step failed and was fixed.** My first attempt errored because the hole-position expression mixed a unitless width with "20 mm". I rewrote the expressions as `(Params.Width / 2 ∓ 20) * 1 mm`, and the second run worked. No export steps failed.

The `/lab/out` folder is on the machine where FreeCAD runs, which may not be this Windows machine. I created it if it was missing.
